##  {.tabset}

### Intro

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,    # hide code
  message = FALSE, # hide messages
  warning = FALSE  # hide warnings
)

library(mclust)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(corrplot)
```

We conducted latent profile analysis, using seven ROAR measures all
tranformed into the ROAR-Word scale in logits. Initial dataset includes
2,224 students in grades 2-8. We subsetted it to include a total of
1,504 students in **grades 2-5** who completed all seven ROAR-measures.

For this analysis **ROAR-sentence** is dropped as it is on its own scale. All the remaining seven ROAR measures are transformed onto the ROAR-Word logit scale. We used this scale (rather than the z-score scale) in the LPA analysis. 

```{r write-out-anonymized-data}
# Load in raw data and write out a simplified and totally de-identified data frame
# Note using updated datafile from Youngsun (sent via email 04-24-26)
df <- read_csv("data/reading_profile_data_deidentified_demo_2026-04-24.csv")

# library(summarytools)
# view(dfSummary(df))
# view(dfSummary(df.mclust))


# pick transformed vars
varnames <- c("word_theta", "phonics_theta_trans" ,"phoneme_theta_trans", "morphology_theta_trans", "cva_theta_trans", "trog_theta_trans", "inference_theta_trans", "sentence_score", "age_months_at_run", "user_grade_at_run") 

# pick original vars
var_original <- c("word_theta", "phonics_theta" ,"phoneme_theta", "morphology_theta", "cva_theta", "trog_theta", "inference_theta", "sentence_score", "age_months_at_run", "user_grade_at_run") 

# create transformed df
roar_df <- df %>% select(all_of(varnames)) %>%
  round(digits=2)
roar_df$id <- factor(df$id)
roar_df <- roar_df %>% 
  select(id, everything())

# create demograph df
demo_df <- df %>% 
  mutate(id = factor(id),
         low_ses = ifelse(socioeconomic_disadvantage == 1, "yes", "no")) %>%  
  select(id,
         grade = user_grade_at_run,
         gender, 
         race.ethnicity = race_cleaned,
         low_ses,
         ell_status, iep_status,
         home_language) 
```

### Samples

```{r demography}
# demographic table (all grades)
library(gtsummary)
demo_df %>%  
  select(-id) %>% 
  tbl_summary(missing_text = "(Missing)") %>% 
   bold_labels() %>% 
  modify_caption("**Table. Student Demographics (all students)**")

# demographic table (grades 2-5)
demo_df %>%  
  select(-id) %>% 
  filter(grade < 6) %>% 
  tbl_summary(missing_text = "(Missing)") %>% 
   bold_labels() %>% 
  modify_caption("**Table. Student Demographics (grades 2-5)**")
```

```{r data-prep}
# create a new matrix with the variables used for clustering and removing any row with 
# an NAN and filtering to grades 2-5
df.mclust8 <- 
  filter(df, user_grade_at_run>=2) %>%
  filter(user_grade_at_run<=5) %>%
  select(varnames[1:8]) 

df.mclust8_orig <- 
  filter(df, user_grade_at_run>=2) %>%
  filter(user_grade_at_run<=5) %>%
  select(var_original[1:8]) 

df.mclust7 <- 
  filter(df, user_grade_at_run>=2) %>%
  filter(user_grade_at_run<=5) %>%
  select(varnames[1:7]) 


# zscore grades 2-5 df with 8 measures including sentence
# because sentence is on a different scale, standardize
# scaling data: all ROAR scores on the z-score scale
scaled_scores_na <- df.mclust8 %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~as.numeric(scale(.))))

scaled_scores_na_orig <- df.mclust8_orig %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~as.numeric(scale(.))))
```

### Correlation

Figure 1 shows a correlation matrix among the eight ROAR measures.

```{r corr_mat, fig.cap="**Figure 1.** *Correlations among eight ROAR measures (N = 1504)*"}
# compute correlation matrix and visualize
c = cor(scaled_scores_na)
corrplot(c, 
         method = 'circle', 
         type = 'lower',    # To show lower half only
         order = 'hclust',  # Keeps the hierarchical clustering order
         addCoef.col = "black", 
         diag = FALSE,          # to hide the diagonal
         number.cex = 0.6, 
         number.digits = 2)
```

```{r corr_mat_tbl7}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(kableExtra)
library(psych) # Useful for getting the formatted correlation matrix

# 1. Define the expert order and clean names for the table
expert_order <- c("inference_theta_trans", "morphology_theta_trans",
                  "cva_theta_trans", "trog_theta_trans",
                  "sentence_score", "word_theta", 
                  "phonics_theta_trans", "phoneme_theta_trans")

clean_labels <- c("1. Inference", "2. Morphology", "3. Vocabulary (CVA)", 
                 "4. Grammar (TROG)", "5. Sentence", 
                 "6. Word Reading", "7. Phonics", "8. Phonemes")

# 2. Extract stats: Means and SDs 
# Assuming df.mclust_na contains the original scores
descriptives <- df.mclust8 %>%
  select(all_of(expert_order)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), 
                   list(M = ~mean(., na.rm=T), 
                        SD = ~sd(., na.rm=T)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), 
               names_to = c("Variable", ".value"), 
               names_pattern = "(.*)_(.*)") %>%
  mutate(Variable = 
           factor(Variable, levels = expert_order)) %>%
  arrange(Variable)

# 3. Create the correlation matrix (Lower Triangle)
cor_mat <- cor(scaled_scores_na[, expert_order])
cor_mat[upper.tri(cor_mat, diag = TRUE)] <- NA # Clean upper triangle

# 4. Combine into final table format
apa_table_display <- as.data.frame(cor_mat) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~sprintf("%.2f", .))) %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~replace(., . == "NA", ""))) %>%
  mutate(Variable = clean_labels,
         M = round(descriptives$M, 2),
         SD = round(descriptives$SD, 2)) %>%
  select(Variable, M, SD, everything()) %>% 
  # Drop the last empty correlation column
  select(1:(ncol(.)-1))

# 3. Generate the clean, professional APA table
apa_table_display %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 2. Descriptive Statistics and Intercorrelations Among ROAR Measures",
      col.names = c("Measure", "M", "SD", 1:7),
      align = "lrrccccccc",
      # --- THE CRITICAL FIX ---
      row.names = FALSE) %>% 
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Times New Roman") %>%
  add_indent(c(1:8)) %>%
  footnote(general = "N = 1,504. Correlations are based on standardized scores. 0.00 indicates the sample average for theta estimates.")

# 5. Generate professional HTML table
# apa_table_df %>%
#   kbl(caption = "Table 1. Descriptive Statistics and Intercorrelations Among ROAR Measures",
#       col.names = c("Assessment Measure", "M", "SD", 1:8),
#       align = "lrrcccccccc") %>%
#   kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Times New Roman") %>%
#   footnote(general = "N = 1,504. Correlations are based on standardized scores, while M and SD are on the ROAR-Word logit scale except for the Sentence measure.")
```

### Latent Profile Analysis

```{r lpa-model-1, echo=FALSE}
# Following these instructions for latent profile analysis https://willhipson.netlify.app/post/latent-profile/latent-profile/ 

# consider tidyLPA instead https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/tidyLPA/vignettes/Introduction_to_tidyLPA.html

# getting and plotting Bayesian Information Criteria 

BIC <- mclustBIC(df.mclust7)
```

#### Exploratory Model Selection (mclust)

We sought to identify optimal student subgroups by conducting a Latent
Profile Analysis (LPA) using the Mclust function within the *mclust*
package in R. This package utilizes a Gaussian Mixture Modeling
framework to identify unobserved (latent) groups within the data. 

```{r bic-plot, fig.cap="**Figure 2.** *BIC Model Selection Plot. Higher values indicate better fit. The 3-profile VVE model (purple line) was selected as the optimal balance of fit and parsimony.*"}
plot(BIC)
```

```{r bic-summary}
# 1. Grab the top row of the summary table
summary(BIC)
bic_summary <- summary(BIC) %>% as.data.frame()

# 2. Extract the model name and number of profiles (e.g., "VVE" and 4)
# The rownames of the summary hold the label "VVE,4"
winning_label <- rownames(bic_summary)[1] 

# 3. Extract the actual BIC value (least negative)
# We use max() because mclust BIC values are negative (higher is better)
best_bic_val <- max(bic_summary$x, na.rm = TRUE)
```

A comparison of fit indices (see below) revealed that the VVE
**(Variable volume, Variable shape, Equal orientation)** model structure
consistently outperformed other specifications. The absolute best statistical fit was achieved by the `r winning_label` model, which yielded a BIC of `r format(round(best_bic_val, 2), big.mark=",")`. 

**Validation via Integrated Completed Likelihood (ICL)**

```{r icl}
# double check we chose the best model by looking at Integrated Completed Likelihood 
ICL <- mclustICL(df.mclust7)
```

```{r icl_plot, fig.cap="**Figure 3.** *BIC Model Selection Plot. Higher values indicate better fit. The 3-profile VVE model (purple line) was selected as the optimal balance of fit and parsimony.*"}
plot(ICL)
```

```{r icl_sum}
summary(ICL)
icl_summary <- summary(ICL) %>% as.data.frame()

# 2. Extract the model name and number of profiles (e.g., "VVE" and 4)
# The rownames of the summary hold the label "VVE,4"
winning_icl <- rownames(icl_summary)[1] 

# 3. Extract the actual BIC value (least negative)
# We use max() because mclust BIC values are negative (higher is better)
best_icl_val <- max(icl_summary$x, na.rm = TRUE)
```

To further validate the number of profiles, we examined the Integrated Completed Likelihood (ICL). While BIC can sometimes favor more complex models, ICL includes an additional penalty for "classification entropy" (how clearly students are assigned to a single group).

As shown in the ICL Model Selection Plot (Figure 3), fit indices for may of the top-performing model structures reached a distinct peak at the 3- or 4-profile solution.

The absolute best statistical fit according to ICL was achieved by the `r winning_icl` model, which yielded a ICL of `r format(round(best_icl_val, 2), big.mark=",")`.

### VVE:3-profiles

The **VVE (Variable volume, Variable shape, Equal orientation)** model allows each profile to have a different number of students (i.e., variable volume) as well as a different variance (i.e., variable shape) while it assumes the seven ROAR measures to correlate and these correlations are invariant across the profiles (i.e., equal orientation).

```{r vve_3_profiles}
#choosing VVE, 3 which is a top model based on BIC
mod_vve3 <- Mclust(df.mclust7, modelNames = "VVE", G = 3)
#summary(mod_vve3)

# Class counts
counts <- table(mod_vve3$classification)

# Calculate percentages from the classification results
class_proportions <- prop.table(table(mod_vve3$classification)) * 100
class_proportions <- round(class_proportions, 1) # Round to 1 decimal

# Display them to check
# print(class_proportions)

# Create the specific labels
# Note: Ensure the Class numbers match your specific plot lines
# Recalculate labels with the "X" prefix to match the dataframe
labels_new <- c(
  "X1" = paste0("Class 1 (", class_proportions["1"], "%)"),
  "X3" = paste0("Class 2 (", class_proportions["3"], "%)"),
  "X2" = paste0("Class 3 (esp. Grammar & Phonics) (", class_proportions["2"], "%)")
)

# final check Boostrap Likelihood Ratio Test (BLRT) -- takes a long time to run do not run unless necessary 
#mclustBootstrapLRT(scores_na, modelName = "VVV")
```
The 3-profile VVE model successfully categorized the `r format(mod_vve3$n, big.mark=",")` students into distinct subgroups. The largest subgroup (Profile 3, $n =$ `r counts["3"]`) represented `r class_proportions["3"]`% of the sample, followed by Profile 1 ($n =$ `r counts["1"]`, `r class_proportions["1"]`%). A smaller, distinct subgroup was also identified (Profile 2, $n =$ `r counts["2"]`, `r class_proportions["2"]`%), representing a specialized pattern of reading development. The high ICL value (`r format(round(mod_vve3$icl, 2), big.mark=",")`) confirms that these three groups are well-separated with high classification
certainty.


```{r visualize-lpa, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Define the new expert-driven order
order <- c("inference_theta_trans", "morphology_theta_trans", "cva_theta_trans",
           "trog_theta_trans", "word_theta", 
           "phonics_theta_trans", "phoneme_theta_trans")

# Update the means dataframe
means <- data.frame(mod_vve3$parameters$mean) %>%
  rownames_to_column() %>%
  rename(Scores = rowname) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(X1, X2, X3), names_to = "Profile", values_to = "Mean") %>%
  mutate(Mean = round(Mean, 2)) %>%
  # --- This is the critical line: re-leveling the factor ---
  mutate(Scores = factor(Scores, levels = order))
```

Figure 3 shows the strength and weakness of the three latent profiles on
the seven ROAR-measures.

```{r profile_plot_vve3, fig.width=10, fig.height=5, fig.cap="**Figure 3.** *Three-Latent Profiles of Reading and Language Skills (VVE). Scores are transformed onto the ROAR-Word logit scale*"}
library(stringr)

vve.c3 <- ggplot(means, aes(x=Scores, y=Mean, group = Profile, color = Profile)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  
  # CLEAN X-AXIS
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) stringr::str_replace_all(x, "_trans|_theta", "")) +
  
  # THE FIX: Add "X" to the keys here
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("X1" = "#2ca02c", "X3" = "#ff7f0e", "X2" = "#d62728"), 
    breaks = c("X1", "X3", "X2"), 
    labels = labels_new
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "logit (ROAR-Word)",
    x = "ROAR Measures"
  )

vve.c3.titles <- vve.c3 + 
  labs(
    title = "VVE: 3-Profile Solution",
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1))


vve.c3.titles

```

**Profile 1 (Green): "The Proficient Readers" (\~43% of sample)**

The Pattern: A relatively flat line among inference, morphology and
vocabulary (CVA), while grammar (trog) creating a valley and word
creating a hill; the means for the 3 foundational skills (word, phonics,
and phoneme) are all higher than those of the comp measures (inference,
morphology, cva and trog).

**Profile 3 (Orange): "The Average Readers" (\~49% of sample)**

The Pattern: A relatively flat line with phoneme being the lowest,
followed by inference.

**Profile 2 (Rd): "The Struggling Readers (esp. Grammar & Phonics" (\~8% of sample)**

The Pattern: All lower than the other two profiles with distinct valleys
with trog and phonics, indicating these students struggle mostly with
receptive grammar and decoding. Interesting to note that these students' relative strenght in Word reading and language comprehension
skills, compared to trog, phonics, and phoneme, and these three measures involve listening to audio. 

```{mclust_other_mods}
# --- 1. Extract the two contenders ---
mod_vve4 <- Mclust(df.mclust7, G = 4, modelNames = "VVE")
mod_vvv3 <- Mclust(df.mclust7, G = 3, modelNames = "VVV")
mod_vvv4 <- Mclust(df.mclust7, G = 4, modelNames = "VVV")

# --- 2. Compare Log-Likelihood and Entropy ---
# Use the function we discussed earlier to calculate entropy for both
# Higher entropy (>0.80) is the goal
calc_entropy <- function(m) {
  n <- nrow(m$z); k <- ncol(m$z)
  return(1 + (sum(m$z * log(m$z + 1e-10)) / (n * log(k))))
}

```{r profile_plot_func}
plot_roar_profiles <- function(mclust_model, 
                               var_order, 
                               class_labels_map, 
                               class_colors, # NEW: User-defined color vector
                               title = "LPA Profile Plot",
                               subtitle = "") {
  
  library(tidyverse)
  library(stringr)

  # 1. Calculate class percentages from the model
  counts <- table(mclust_model$classification)
  proportions <- round(prop.table(counts) * 100, 1)
  
  # 2. Extract means and reshape
  means_df <- as.data.frame(mclust_model$parameters$mean) %>%
    rownames_to_column(var = "Scores") %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = starts_with("V"),
      names_to = "Profile",
      values_to = "Mean"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Mean = round(Mean, 2),
      Scores = factor(Scores, levels = var_order),
      # Ensure Profile matches the "X1" format used in your mapping
      Profile = str_replace(Profile, "V", "X")
    )

  # 3. Create dynamic labels (Name + %)
  # This matches the names in class_labels_map to the calculated proportions
  final_labels <- sapply(names(class_labels_map), function(x) {
    class_num <- str_replace(x, "X", "")
    paste0(class_labels_map[x], " (", proportions[class_num], "%)")
  })

  # 4. Build Plot
  ggplot(means_df, aes(x = Scores, y = Mean, group = Profile, color = Profile)) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) str_replace_all(x, "_trans|_theta", "")) +
    
    # USE USER-DEFINED COLORS AND LABELS
    scale_color_manual(
      values = class_colors,      # Directly use your color vector
      breaks = names(class_labels_map), # Force legend order
      labels = final_labels       # Use the name + % labels
    ) +
    
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_blank()
    ) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, y = "logit (ROAR-Word)", x = "ROAR Measures")
}
```

### VVE:4-profiles

The **VVE (Variable volume, Variable shape, Equal orientation)** model allows each profile to have a different number of students (i.e., variable volume) as well as a different variance (i.e., variable shape) while it assumes the seven ROAR measures to correlate and these correlations are invariant across the profiles (i.e., equal orientation).

Figure 4 shows the strength and weakness of the three latent profiles on
the seven ROAR-measures.

```{r profile_plot_vve4, fig.width=10, fig.height=5, fig.cap="**Figure 4.** *Four-Latent Profiles of Reading and Language Skills (VVE). Scores are transformed onto the ROAR-Word logit scale (N = 1504)*"}

  "X1" = "Proficient",
  "X3" = "Above Average", # Swapped: X3 is the 2nd highest line
  "X4" = "Developing",    # Swapped: X4 is the 3rd highest line
  "X2" = "Struggling (Dual-Focus)"
)

  "X3" = "#377eb8", # Blue (2nd)
  "X4" = "#ff7f0e", # Orange (3rd)
  "X2" = "#d62728"  # Red (Bottom)
)


# 3. Call your function (assuming you updated the internal function to handle Blue)
mod_vve4 <- Mclust(df.mclust7, G = 4, modelNames = "VVE")
vve4_plot <-

vve4_plot

### Multi-group LPA

We conducted the multigroup Latent Profile Analysis (MGLPA) to examine
whether the four-profile structure is invarianet between two grade-bands:
grades 2-3 and grades 4-5. The MGLPA results are summarized in Table 4.
The 3-profile solution from the VVV model demonstrated robust statistical fit and high
classification clarity (Entropy = 0.83). The Bootstrap Likelihood Ratio
Test ($p < .01$) confirmed that the 5-profile structure significantly
outperformed the 2-profile model. Notably, the smallest identified
subgroup represented 8.7% of the total sample, ensuring sufficient group
stability for comparing developmental patterns across grade-bands.

```{r data_prep_multi}
# Create the two developmental groups
df.groups <- df %>%
  filter(user_grade_at_run < 6) %>% 
  mutate(grade_group = ifelse(user_grade_at_run <= 3, 
                              "Grades 2-3", "Grades 4-5"))

df.mclust7.grp <- df.mclust7
df.mclust7.grp$grade_group <- df.groups$grade_group

dat_numeric <- df.mclust7.grp %>%
  select(all_of(order))

group_vector <- df.mclust7.grp$grade_group
```

```{r multiG_LPA_fits}
library(tidyLPA)
# Estimate the 5-profile model across groups
# We use 'estimate_profiles' with the 'group' argument
mg_lpa <- dat_numeric %>%
  estimate_profiles(n_profiles = 3, 
                    package = "mclust", 
                    model_names = "VVV",
                    group = group_vector) 

# Get results
fit_stats <- get_fit(mg_lpa) 


library(dplyr)
library(kableExtra)

# Select and clean the columns for the report
mg_table_clean <- fit_stats %>%
  select(Classes, LogLik, BIC, Entropy, n_min, BLRT_p) %>%
  mutate(
    # Convert n_min to a more readable percentage
    n_min = paste0(round(n_min * 100, 1), "%"),
    # Round the large stats
    across(c(LogLik, BIC, Entropy), ~round(., 2))
  )

# Create the professional HTML table
mg_table_clean %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 4. Fit Indices for Multigroup Latent Profile Analysis (N=1,504)",
      col.names = c("Profiles", "Log-Likelihood", "BIC", "Entropy", "Smallest Class %", "BLRT (p)"),
      align = "c") %>%
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Arial") %>%
  # THE FIX: Add the kableExtra:: prefix
  kableExtra::footnote(general = "Note: BIC: Bayesian Information Criterion; BLRT: Bootstrap Likelihood Ratio Test.")
```

#### Profile Plots

```{r mg_profile_line_plots}

mg_data <- get_data(mg_lpa)
mg_data$group <- group_vector

# --- 2. Manually calculate M & se for each Class WITHIN each Group
mg_plot_data_with_se <- mg_data %>%
  # Pivot assessment columns to a long format
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(order), names_to = "Parameter", values_to = "Score") %>%
  group_by(group, Class, Parameter) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Estimate = mean(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Calculate Standard Error: SD / sqrt(n)
    se = sd(Score, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Re-apply your expert storytelling order
  mutate(Parameter = factor(Parameter, levels = order))

# --- 3. Plot with Faceting by Grade Group ---
# Define colors to match your bar chart (2 = Red/Struggling)
mg_colors <- c("1"="#2ca02c", "2"="#d62728", "3"="#1f77b4", "4"="#ff7f0e")

ggplot(mg_plot_data_with_se, aes(x = Parameter, y = Mean_Estimate, 
                                 group = factor(Class), color = factor(Class))) +
  # Add Error Bars FIRST so they sit behind the points
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean_Estimate - 1.96*se, 
                    ymax = Mean_Estimate + 1.96*se), 
                width = 0.2, alpha = 0.4) + 
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~group) + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) str_remove(x, "_.*")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = mg_colors) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Reading Profiles: Lower- vs. Upper-Grade Band Comparison with 95% CI",
    y = "logit (ROAR-Word)",
    x = NULL
  )

### Dimensionality Analysis

Parallel analysis indicated a clear unidimensional structure, with only the first factor exceeding the eigenvalues generated from simulated and resampled data (Figure 1). This suggests that a single primary dimension of 'General Reading Ability' accounts for the majority of the variance in the 7 ROAR measures.

```{r efa}
library(psych)
# 1. Determine how many factors to extract (Parallel Analysis)
# This is the 'BIC plot' equivalent for EFA
# fa.parallel(scaled_scores_na, fa = "fa")
fa.parallel(df.mclust7, fa = "fa")
```

#### Factor Structure and Construct Integration

```{r factor_structure}

# Run the EFA
# We use 'oblimin' rotation because we expect Language and Code to correlate
efa_results <- fa(df.mclust7, 
                  nfactors = 2, rotate = "oblimin")

# 3. Look at the loadings
print(efa_results$loadings, cutoff = 0)


# --- Extracting EFA Results for Dynamic Reporting ---

# Variance Explained
# Vaccounted contains SS loadings, Proportion Var, etc.
efa_summary <- efa_results$Vaccounted

f1_prop_var <- round(efa_summary["Proportion Var", "MR1"] * 100, 1)
f2_prop_var <- round(efa_summary["Proportion Var", "MR2"] * 100, 1)
f2_eigen    <- round(efa_summary["SS loadings", "MR2"], 2)

# Factor 1 Loading Range
# We grab the first column of the loadings matrix
f1_loadings <- as.numeric(efa_results$loadings[, 1])
f1_min <- round(min(f1_loadings), 2)
f1_max <- round(max(f1_loadings), 2)

# Specific Target Loadings (for the story)
# Use the exact row names from your dataframe
loadings_mat <- as.data.frame(unclass(efa_results$loadings))

morph_f1   <- round(loadings_mat["morphology_theta_trans", "MR1"], 2)
vocab_f1   <- round(loadings_mat["cva_theta_trans", "MR1"], 2)
phoneme_f2 <- round(loadings_mat["phoneme_theta_trans", "MR2"], 2)
```
The Exploratory Factor Analysis conducted on aligned logit scores revealed two distinct dimensions of reading ability. Factor loadings were evaluated using a substantive threshold of .30 (Comrey & Lee, 1992). Factor 1 (Linguistic Comprehension) accounted for `r f1_prop_var`% of the common variance and was defined by strong primary loadings ranging from `r f1_min` to `r f1_max`. This factor was most strongly anchored by morphological awareness ($loading =$ `r morph_f1`) and academic vocabulary ($loading =$ `r vocab_f1`).

Factor 2 (Structural Mechanics) accounted for an additional `r f2_prop_var`% of the variance. With an eigenvalue of `r f2_eigen`, this factor reached the standard threshold for substantive significance and was primarily defined by phoneme awareness ($loading =$ `r phoneme_f2`). These results provide the theoretical justification for our subsequent person-centered analysis, as they demonstrate that structural and linguistic skills represent distinct axes of developmental growth, particularly with the lowest performing profile.

```{r efa_loading_tbl}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(flextable)
library(officer) # For border styling

# 1. Prepare the Data Programmatically
label_map <- c(
  "inference_theta_trans"   = "Inference",
  "morphology_theta_trans"  = "Morphology",
  "cva_theta_trans"         = "Vocabulary (CVA)",
  "trog_theta_trans"        = "Grammar (TROG)",
  "word_theta"              = "Word Reading",
  "phonics_theta_trans"     = "Phonics",
  "phoneme_theta_trans"     = "Phoneme Awareness"
)

loadings_part <- as.data.frame(unclass(efa_results$loadings)) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("RawName") %>%
  mutate(Measure = label_map[RawName]) %>%
  select(Measure, MR1, MR2)

summary_part <- as.data.frame(efa_results$Vaccounted) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Measure") %>%
  mutate(Measure = case_when(
    Measure == "SS loadings" ~ "SS Loadings (Eigenvalues)",
    Measure == "Proportion Var" ~ "Proportion Variance",
    Measure == "Cumulative Var" ~ "Cumulative Variance",
    TRUE ~ Measure
  )) %>%
  select(Measure, MR1, MR2)

efa_final_df <- bind_rows(loadings_part, summary_part)

# 2. Define standard APA border (regular thickness = 1pt)
std_border <- fp_border(color = "black", width = 1)

# 3. Create the Flextable
ft <- flextable(efa_final_df) %>%
  # Round numbers and handle NAs for the summary text
  colformat_double(digits = 3) %>%
  set_header_labels(Measure = "Assessment Measure", MR1 = "Factor 1", MR2 = "Factor 2") %>%
  
  # Professional APA Styling
  font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") %>%
  fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") %>%
  border_remove() %>%
  hline_top(border = std_border, part = "header") %>%
  hline_bottom(border = std_border, part = "header") %>%
  hline_bottom(border = std_border, part = "body") %>%
  
  # DYNAMIC BOLDING: Bolds loadings > 0.40
  bold(i = ~ MR1 > 0.3, j = 2) %>%
  bold(i = ~ MR2 > 0.3, j = 3) %>%
  
  # Add the horizontal line before summary stats (row 7 is the last measure)
  hline(i = 7, border = std_border) %>%
  
  # Add Footnote
  add_footer_lines("Note. Extraction method: minimum residual with Oblimin rotation. Factor 1: Linguistic Comprehension; Factor 2: Structural Mechanics, involving audio listening") %>%
  font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "footer") %>%
  fontsize(size = 9, part = "footer") %>%
  
  autofit()

ft

# 4. Export to Word
# save_as_docx(ft, path = "output/EFA_Loadings_Table.docx")

```
